title: Gamified Apps and the Speaking Gap: August 2026
summary: Swain's Output Hypothesis explains why Duolingo won't make you fluent. Build a speaking-first study stack that works in August 2026.
body_text: Keeping a streak going feels like progress, and for a while that holds true. But at some point the tiles and word banks stop moving you forward, and every real conversation still feels like a test you haven't studied for. The gap between what you can decode and what you can actually say out loud has a specific cause, and fixing it means practicing the thing Duolingo structurally cannot ask you to do. TLDR: Duolingo builds vocabulary recognition at A1 and A2, but most users hit a ceiling around low B1 because the app optimizes for daily engagement, not spoken output production. Swain's Output Hypothesis (1985) explains why: comprehension lets you infer meaning from context, while speaking forces you to conjugate verbs, pick prepositions, and sequence clauses under pressure you can't shortcut. Duolingo Max's Roleplay runs on scaffolded paths that circle back to safe questions when you drift, which builds confidence but leaves the core production gap intact past B1. A speaking-first study stack pairs daily AI voice reps with a human tutor on italki or Preply every one to two weeks to catch the errors that reps alone won't surface. ISSEN is an AI voice tutor that delivers open-ended, unscripted conversations with in-turn correction and hands-free background mode, priced at $20 to $29 USD per month as one input inside a broader study plan. What gamified apps actually do well Gamified apps get a bad rap in speaking-focused corners of the internet, and some of that criticism is deserved. Some of it isn't. Before we get to what Duolingo cannot do, it helps to name what it does well, because a lot of readers still open the app every morning. Where these apps genuinely earn their place: Daily habit formation. Streaks, notifications, and five-minute lessons solve the hardest problem in adult learning, which is showing up on the days you don't feel like it. Passive vocabulary at A1 and A2. Tapping through short exercises builds recognition of high-frequency words faster than most language learning apps for speaking . A near-zero barrier to starting. No placement test, no schedule, no tutor to book. These are real gains, and they are prerequisites for conversational fluency. Learners who can't recognize the top 500 words have nothing to draw on when a real conversation starts. Is Duolingo enough to become fluent? Short answer: no. If your goal is real conversation, Duolingo alone will not get you there, and no streak extension changes that. The reason is structural. The app is built around 5 to 10 minutes a day of tapping tiles, which keeps a habit alive and grows recognition of common words, but sits nowhere near the spoken output volume conversational fluency requires. Most users hit a familiar ceiling around A2 or low B1: they can read a Duolingo sentence, follow a slow podcast, and still freeze when a barista asks a follow-up question, which is why speaking practice belongs in your routine . That gap between what you decode and what you produce is the plateau. Adding more lessons on the same side of the equation does not close it. Why doesn't gamification produce speaking ability? Gamification optimizes for the metric it can measure, which is daily engagement. Acquisition optimizes for productive difficulty: friction, gaps, and moments where you cannot find the word. When a product team has to choose between the two every sprint, engagement wins. That choice shows up in three mechanics: Multiple choice removes active retrieval. Picking a tile from four options is recognition work, not the cold production speaking demands. Word banks skip sentence construction under pressure. Dragging pre-set tiles into order bypasses assembling a clause from memory while someone waits. Streaks reward showing up, not stretching. A five-minute review protects the streak; a harder conversation moves you forward and feels bad in a way apps cannot afford to feel, and that friction is part of what makes a language app immersive . Swain's Output Hypothesis (1985) predicts this: learners notice gaps only when forced to produce language, not select it from a menu. The difference between recognition and production in language learning Merrill Swain developed the Output Hypothesis (1985) after watching something strange in Canadian French immersion programs. Students had years of rich input from native-speaking teachers, and their listening comprehension climbed close to native levels. Their speaking did not. They understood everything and produced sentences riddled with gaps no comprehension test would catch. Swain's diagnosis: comprehension runs on semantic shortcuts. You infer meaning from context, cognates, and one or two anchor words per sentence, without ever parsing the full grammar. Production has nowhere to hide. To say a sentence out loud, you have to choose a subject, conjugate a verb, pick the right preposition, and sequence the whole thing before your listener loses patience. That forced assembly surfaces the gaps, and that assembly work no tile-tapping session asks you to do. Swain called this the "noticing function" of output. Does Duolingo Max fix the speaking problem in 2026? Duolingo Max is the fair test of whether the gamified category can close the production gap. At $29.99 per month or $168 per year (verify current pricing on Duolingo's site before subscribing), the tier gives you Video Call with Lily and Roleplay scenarios in Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, and Korean, with Explain My Answer free for all users as of January 2026 (verify on duolingo.com). For an A2 learner who has never spoken a full sentence out loud, Video Call with Lily is a real upgrade. You get a face, a voice, and a low-stakes prompt loop. Roleplay adds scripted scenarios like ordering coffee, with the tutor holding your hand through predictable turns. The ceiling shows up around B1. Roleplay runs on scaffolded paths: Lily circles back to safe questions when you drift, and exchanges are shaped so you rarely produce a sentence the system did not anticipate. Helpful for confidence, useless for the skill you plateau on, which is assembling language under pressure you cannot predict. That is precisely where AI language tutoring for speaking fluency opens a different path. What to use instead of a gamified app Four categories cover most of what works after you outgrow tile-tapping. Each fixes a different piece of the production gap, and none solves the whole thing alone. Category What it gives you Where it falls short AI voice tutors On-demand reps, unlimited turns, low cost per session, unpredictable prompts Cannot replace deep cultural feedback or long-term human accountability Human tutors (italki, Preply) Real cultural correction, scheduled accountability, targeted work on fossilized errors $15 to $40 per session makes daily practice financially painful Immersion (media, environment) Rich input, natural register, exposure to slang and idiom Passive by default; input without forced output leaves the plateau intact Language exchange partners Free, real humans, cultural exchange Scheduling friction, uneven skill levels, no correction discipline A 2024 AI chatbot speaking practice review found benefits for anxiety reduction, confidence, and speaking outcomes, with the strongest evidence in low-stakes contexts. The practical read: AI tutors handle daily reps, and human tutors handle periodic correction of errors reps alone will not surface. How to build a speaking-first study stack in 2026 A speaking-first stack layers daily AI voice reps, weekly or monthly human correction, and passive input as background listening. Past A2, treat unscripted output as your primary metric. Verify pricing and beta status on each product's site before subscribing. App Unscripted speaking Real-time correction Hands-free Monthly price ISSEN Yes, open-ended voice Yes, in-turn Yes, background mode $20 to $29 Duolingo No No No Free or $14 Super Duolingo Max Scripted Roleplay only Explain My Answer post-turn No $29.99 Babbel Babbel Speak in beta , mobile only Beta, verify scope No Verify on live site Busuu Community written feedback Delayed peer review No Verify on live site Memrise MemBot chat, mostly text No No Verify on live site Pair one voice tool for daily reps with a human tutor on italki or Preply every one to two weeks for correction on patterns the AI misses. The AI vs. human tutor speaking tradeoffs are worth understanding before you commit. How ISSEN fills the gap gamified apps leave ISSEN is an AI voice tutor built around the one thing gamified apps structurally cannot deliver: unscripted spoken output under real-time pressure. Difficulty, vocabulary, and speaking pace adapt inside a single session, a hallmark of personalized language learning apps , and progress is measured in minutes of spoken output instead of streaks. ISSEN is one input inside a broader study plan, not a replacement for grammar work or real-world exposure. For a broader comparison, see the best AI language tutors for conversation practice . Smart turn detection means no push-to-talk. You speak, the tutor waits, and the exchange runs closer to a real conversation than a walkie-talkie. Background and lock-screen mode turns a walk or commute into speaking reps without staring at the app. Conversation-anchored SRS surfaces words inside the sentences you actually said, so review carries the grammatical frame you built them in, one feature among many in the best apps for language fluency . 60+ languages, flat monthly pricing of $20 to $29 USD, no per-session math. Final thoughts on why Duolingo doesn't make you fluent Gamified apps solve a real problem: they get you to show up. What they cannot solve is the production gap, because tapping tiles and speaking under pressure are different cognitive tasks entirely. Your reading level and your speaking level will stay mismatched until you add regular, unscripted spoken output to your stack. Think about Mia, a logistics coordinator in Warsaw who hit B1 in Spanish after eight months of Duolingo but still freezes on customer calls with her company's new Mexico City office. Her goal: handle a 5-minute supplier call in Spanish without blanking by Q4 2026. She can read an email in Spanish without hesitating. She cannot get through a two-minute phone call without her mind blanking mid-sentence. That gap, between what she decodes and what she produces under pressure, is exactly what Swain's Output Hypothesis predicted in 1985, and that gap is what AI voice tutors are now positioned to close at scale. In two to three years, a tutor like ISSEN will know Mia's job vocabulary, her recurring error patterns from the last 30 sessions, and the fact that her next call is on Thursday. Daily reps will feel less like practice and more like prep for a specific conversation she is about to have. The principle is the same one Swain described; the friction, the cost, the scheduling, the lack of a patient interlocutor, is what keeps getting removed. Try ISSEN free for 10 minutes and see how different daily voice reps feel from daily review. FAQs Why doesn't Duolingo make you fluent even after months of consistent practice? The problem is structural, not motivational. Duolingo is built around 5-10 minutes of daily tile-tapping, which trains word recognition but never asks you to produce a sentence from memory under conversational pressure. Swain's Output Hypothesis (1985) explains why that matters: gaps in your grammar and syntax only surface when you're forced to speak, not when you're selecting from a menu of options. What should I use instead of Duolingo Max when I've hit the B1 plateau? Duolingo Max's Roleplay feature helps at A2, but its scaffolded paths keep conversations predictable enough that you rarely have to assemble language under real pressure. At B1 and above, you need unscripted spoken output: an AI voice tutor like ISSEN for daily reps, paired with a human tutor on italki or Preply every one to two weeks to catch the errors that volume alone won't fix. Can I build real speaking ability without a human tutor? You can get considerably further than most learners expect, but with a clear caveat: AI voice practice handles the volume problem, not every problem. Daily sessions with an AI tutor build the automaticity that weekly human tutoring sessions can't supply at that frequency. Human tutors on Preply or italki still earn their place for catching fossilized errors and cultural nuance that accumulate over months of practice. How is ISSEN different from Duolingo Max for speaking practice? Duolingo Max offers scripted Roleplay scenarios with post-turn feedback, while ISSEN runs open-ended voice conversations with no push-to-talk mechanics, real-time difficulty adjustment, and background mode so sessions continue during a walk or commute. The structural difference is that ISSEN generates unpredictable conversational pressure: the condition Swain identified as the one that actually forces your brain to notice gaps. What does a speaking-first study stack actually look like in practice? The core structure is daily AI voice reps with a tutor like ISSEN, human correction on italki or Preply every one to two weeks, and passive input like podcasts or TV as background listening. Past A2, treat minutes of spoken output as your primary progress metric, not lessons completed or streak days maintained.

title: Understanding shipping zones: A comprehensive guide for 2025
summary: Understand what shipping zones are and how to reduce costs using network optimization and smart routing. Start scaling today.
body_text: To achieve fast, efficient order fulfillment and network optimization , you need a clear understanding of how shipping zones influence cost and delivery time .For scaling ecommerce brands, this need is even more important: Your ability to evaluate geographic reach, carrier options, and delivery expectations directly impacts your growth.Today's guide breaks down everything you need to know about shipping zones, how they work, and ways to use them to your advantage. What Are Shipping Zones? Shipping zones are geographical areas or segments that carriers (e.g., USPS, UPS, FedEx) use to determine shipping costs and delivery times. Zones typically range between 1 and 8 within the US. The distance between the origin zip code or postal code and the destination defines zones, with lower numbers indicating locations closer to the shipment's origin and higher numbers representing destinations farther away. How Do Carriers Use Shipping Zones? Shipping carriers use a tiered pricing model based on geographic distance from the point of origin. Each carrier has its own network of origin points, so one’s Zone 3 may be another’s Zone 4. You’ll also find that they use shipping zone maps and rate tables to calculate delivery costs, ensuring that every mile traveled is accounted for. Doing so allows carriers to optimize prices and delivery times. For ecommerce businesses, understanding how carriers utilize zones is crucial as it directly impacts your shipping costs. The further your package has to travel, the higher the shipping zone number, and consequently, the more you’ll pay. That said, being strategic about your fulfillment center’s location and carrier options can reduce costs and delivery times. How to Calculate Shipping Zones You determine shipping zones according to the shipping origin, which is within Zone 1, while the destination zone is based on its distance from that point. For example, if your fulfillment center is in southern California, Zone 1 would be another address in the same zip code group, whereas Zone 8 may be a zip code in New York.Carriers like USPS, FedEx, and UPS standardize the distance-based logic of zones and shipping expectations, meaning no exact mileage or border defines each zone universally. Zones generally correlate with distance ranges, but exact ZIP codes included in each zone vary by carrier. Furthermore, carriers may assign different zones depending on the service selected.To simplify matters, most carriers offer free online tools. You can enter your fulfillment center’s and customer’s ZIP codes, and the tool will return the applicable zone.However, this process is tedious and impractical if you’re an ecommerce business with thousands of orders to handle. Utilizing tools like Flowspace’s Network Optimization System (NOS) helps you position your warehouse and fulfillment centers according to your historical data. In return, you can determine the right locations (called nodes) to shorten zone distance, minimize costs, and streamline order fulfillment at scale. How Do Shipping Zones Impact Ecommerce Order Fulfillment? For ecommerce brands, shipping zones affect shipping rates, delivery times, and customer experience. Consequently, understanding how zones work—and how to work around them—can give you a major edge in scaling efficiently. Shipping Costs Think of shipping costs like a balloon: the farther a package travels, the more it expands. As the shipping zone increases, so does the cost, since carriers incur higher expenses over longer distances.Heavier packages amplify this effect, with shipping costs rising more significantly compared to lighter packages. Read More: How Emma Mattress Powered 5X Growth and Conquered the U.S. Market with Flowspace Some carrier services offer flat-rate pricing, where the cost stays the same regardless of distance or weight. While this can simplify budgeting, it’s not always the most cost-effective or practical option if you’re shipping heavier packages that exceed the limit or primarily serve customers in nearby zones.In those cases, shipping from fulfillment centers closer to your customers reduces the number of zones your packages cross and helps you save significantly over time. Delivery Times Shipping zones also have a major impact on delivery times. Naturally, the closer the zone is, the faster the delivery is. As with costs, choosing the right location can significantly reduce transit times and allow most customers to receive their orders within a 1-2 day range. Working with a fulfillment partner helps you achieve this by simplifying your transportation network and strategically positioning your inventory (without having to manage multiple warehouses on your own).Furthermore, your team can use ecommerce fulfillment software to review and adjust your operations to stay ahead of logistics demands , maintain speedy deliveries, and achieve high customer satisfaction. Free Shipping Shipping zones also impact free shipping, a common and beloved incentive. Many customers are willing to purchase more items to qualify for free shipping. However, high shipping costs to farther zones present a challenge.To manage these costs, brands must balance expenses and customer expectations. For instance, you might offer free shipping over a certain order threshold, limit it to specific zones, or include the cost in product pricing. Another option is to partner with a fulfillment provider that helps cut last-mile delivery expenses, making it easier to absorb shipping costs without cutting too deeply into your margins. 4 Strategies to Reduce Shipping Costs To scale, it’s essential to reduce shipping costs where possible, especially in the face of logistical difficulties like global tariffs, carrier rate hikes, and changing customer needs.Here are a few key strategies to help your team out. 1. Use Multiple Fulfillment Centers Splitting inventory across multiple fulfillment centers means shipping to lower zones. This kind of distribution model reduces last-mile delivery costs, which make up 53% of total shipping costs , enables faster shipping options (like 2-day or even same-day delivery), and can help increase conversion rates.For growing ecommerce brands, multiple fulfillment centers provide operational flexibility and scalability. For example, you can meet regional demand spikes without overburdening a single location. To achieve this, modern fulfillment partners like Flowspace offer a unified dashboard and smart order routing. Orders are automatically assigned to the closest warehouse with available inventory to speed up delivery and lower shipping costs. The system also applies business rules to exclude underperforming or high-cost carriers and uses destination-based fulfillment logic to optimize each shipment. Smart tagging and automated exception handling further reduce manual effort, giving your team full control without added complexity. 2. Flat-Rate Shipping Flat-rate shipping is ideal for small packages and long-distance shipments. Since pricing stays the same regardless of distance or weight (within limits), it provides cost predictability and simplifies budgeting.While not always effective for heavy or local deliveries, flat-rate shipping can be a smart addition if it suits your business model and sets concrete expectations for customers. 3. Zone Skipping Zone skipping is a cost-saving strategy where businesses consolidate many packages heading to the same region and ship them in bulk (typically via freight or linehaul) to a carrier nearer to a final destination.From there, a last-mile carrier delivers the individual packages to customers.By avoiding multiple zone-based charges on individual parcels, zone skipping helps reduce per-package shipping costs, especially for high-volume shippers. That said, it may introduce a slight delay compared to direct parcel shipping, but the savings can be significant if you tend to ship large volumes to the same area. 4. Monitor Key Metrics Tracking the right fulfillment and shipping metrics can uncover hidden costs and highlight opportunities to improve zone efficiency. Key indicators include: Average shipping zone per order Cost per zone Delivery time by zone By regularly reviewing this data and automating cost calculations, your team can make smarter decisions around warehouse placement, carrier selection, and service-level offerings. Best Practices for Managing Shipping Zones Effectively managing shipping zones isn’t just about saving on costs. It’s about building a fulfillment strategy that’s scalable, efficient, and customer-friendly.Here are some best practices to guide your approach: Optimize fulfillment node placement based on customer demand: Analyze order data to identify where most of your customers are located, then strategically place fulfillment centers to reduce average shipping zones. This ensures faster deliveries and lower costs. Use a multi-carrier strategy: Don’t rely on just one carrier. Using multiple shipping partners lets you compare rates and transit times by zone, choose the most cost-effective service for each shipment, and build redundancy into your delivery network. Track shipping volume by zone: Regularly monitor how many packages you're sending to each zone. Doing so can reveal regional customer demand and inform both warehouse placement and targeted marketing campaigns. Bundle shipping costs into product pricing for free shipping: Instead of cutting into your margins, account for average zone-based shipping costs in your product pricing. This keeps your shipping promise simple for customers without sacrificing profitability. Strengthen fulfillment processes: Use tools like smart order routing, real-time reports, and shipping label generation to reduce human error, speed up operations, and make data-driven decisions—especially when managing multiple zones and carriers. How Flowspace Helps You Cut Costs Shipping zones are more than just a pricing tool—they're a critical factor in scaling ecommerce operations, controlling costs, and exceeding delivery expectations. From fulfillment node placement to carrier selection, your ability to navigate zone-based logistics will directly impact your margins and your customer experience.Flowspace makes it easy. With tools like the Network Optimization System (NOS) and smart order routing, Flowspace helps you pinpoint ideal warehouse locations and ship from the closest node with inventory. You can also avoid costly carriers and apply destination-based fulfillment rules to reduce costs, improve delivery speed, and maintain a consistent customer experience—all from a single, unified platform.Whether you're just starting to expand your footprint or ready to fully optimize your logistics network, Flowspace gives you the visibility and flexibility to do it right.Ready to simplify zone management and scale smarter? Talk to a fulfillment expert at Flowspace today. FAQs What Are Shipping Zones? Shipping zones are geographic regions that help carriers calculate costs and delivery times based on how far your package has to travel. So, when you’re shipping, remember: where it’s going can change how much it’s costing you. How Do Shipping Zones Affect Shipping Costs? Shipping zones function much like a tiered system—the higher the zone number, the greater the distance, and the higher the cost. As distance increases, so do your shipping expenses, making strategic fulfillment decisions essential for protecting your margins. How Can Multiple Fulfillment Centers Reduce Shipping Costs? Multiple fulfillment centers keep your inventory closer to customers, slashing shipping distances and costs to improve the customer experience.

title: Payroll Services Pricing: Compare Costs and Plans
summary: Payroll services pricing for CPA firms market benchmarks, cost-plus vs bundled models, per-employee vs per-payroll structure, and add-ons that decide profitability.
body_text: Payroll is one of two most common service-line expansions for a CPA firm other is fractional CFO or advisory. Every existing client with employees is a payroll prospect, and every firm eventually decides whether payroll is a pass-through service (client uses Gusto, ADP, or QBO Payroll, firm reconciles) or a billable service line (firm runs payroll and prices it as a monthly recurring engagement). What market charges 2026 benchmarks Two separate price benchmarks matter: what payroll providers charge (firm's cost side) and what CPA firms charge their clients (firm's revenue side). Payroll provider vendor pricing (firm cost): Square Payroll $35/mo base + $6 per employee per month (PEPM). Contractor-only: $6 PEPM, no base. Gusto $40/mo base + $6 PEPM (Simple); $80/mo + $12 PEPM (Plus). QuickBooks Payroll $50–$130/mo base + $6–$11 PEPM depending on tier. ADP RUN quote-based, typically $50–$150/mo base + $4–$12 PEPM for SMB. Paychex Flex quote-based, typically $60–$200/mo base + $4–$15 PEPM. Rippling / Justworks / Deel PEO or advanced HRIS, $8–$30 PEPM (broader scope than payroll only). Small-business "all-in" payroll cost (CPA firm client-side benchmarks): Forbes (Oct 2025): $4–$22 PEPM on top of a base fee. Paychex (Feb 2025): $30–$100 per person per month for full outsourced payroll. HireLevel (Mar 2025): $125–$450/mo total for firms with 25–200 employees. Patriot Software survey: 42% of small businesses pay $101–$500/mo total; 22% pay $51–$100/mo. The CPA-firm-billed price sits above raw vendor cost. The delta is firm's margin on reconciliation, tax filing management, garnishments, year-end forms, and client communication work. The four pricing models Model 1: Cost-plus (pass-through markup). Client pays vendor cost plus a fixed markup (typically 20–40%). Simple, transparent, and works for cost-conscious clients. Downside: margin is thin, and firm's time is not directly compensated when a payroll cycle goes sideways Model 2: Bundled fixed monthly. One flat monthly fee covers vendor cost + processing + tax filing + quarterly returns + year-end. Common range: $200–$600/mo for a 5–15 employee client, $600–$1,500/mo for a 15–50 employee client. Best when client wants predictability and firm has efficient internal workflows. Model 3: Per-payroll flat fee. A fixed fee per payroll run often $75–$200 per bi-weekly run for small clients. Works when payroll frequency varies (weekly restaurants vs. bi-weekly office clients). Downside: incentivizes fewer payroll runs, which is not always what client should do. Model 4: Value-based tier. A tiered menu "Essentials" (payroll + basic tax filing), "Standard" (adds garnishments, multi-state, W-2/1099), "Complete" (adds HR support, benefits administration, workers comp reporting). Common range: $150 / $300 / $600+ per month. Highest gross margin when tiers are engineered around firm's actual delivery cost. Most established CPA firms end up on Model 4 for larger clients and Model 2 for smaller ones . Cost-plus is transitional model when a firm first launches service line. The 12 add-ons that price separately Every payroll engagement should have a base scope and a clear list of add-ons priced à la carte. The 12 most common: Multi-state payroll additional state registration and filing per state, typically $50–$200 per state per month. Multiple pay frequencies running weekly for hourly staff and semi-monthly for salaried adds ~$50/mo. Garnishment processing $25–$50 per active garnishment per month. Child support and levy administration flat fee per order, ~$50–$100 setup, $10–$25/mo ongoing. 401(k) and benefits deduction sync $25–$75/mo depending on provider integration. Workers compensation "pay-as-you-go" $10–$50/mo integration fee. Time and attendance integration $25–$100/mo depending on system. W-2 / 1099 year-end forms either bundled or $5–$10 per form. Quarterly Form 941 filing often bundled; standalone $50–$150 per quarter. State unemployment (SUI) rate management $25–$75 per year per state to update. New hire reporting usually bundled; $10–$25 per new hire if standalone. Owner / S-corp reasonable compensation reviews $150–$400 per year per shareholder. The default is to bundle 1–3 add-ons into base and price everything else separately. Firms that bundle everything into a single fee tend to underprice multi-state and garnishment work, which are two lines that consume most staff time. The break-even math A CPA firm's break-even on payroll depends on hourly delivery cost, not on vendor invoice. Rough model for a 10-employee client on bi-weekly payroll: Vendor cost: $40 base + $6 × 10 = $100/mo Firm labor: ~30 minutes per pay run × 2.17 runs/mo = 1.1 hours + 30 min/mo reconciliation + 15 min/mo client communication = ~1.9 hours/mo At $75/hr fully burdened labor: $143/mo internal cost Total firm cost: ~$243/mo Charge $400/mo bundled: $157/mo margin, ~40% gross margin Add a garnishment ($40/mo), workers comp integration ($25), and multi-state ($150 for a second state) and price is $615 against maybe $340 of cost 45% gross margin. Below $250/mo bundled for a 10-employee client, firm is probably losing money on engagement once quarterly filings and year-end work are counted. That is price floor to guard. What clients actually pay attention to The features that drive client stickiness and therefore pricing power a CPA firm has are not raw price per employee: Direct deposit reliability a missed direct deposit is a client-losing event. Tax filing accuracy a mis-filed 941 or state withholding causes penalty letters that firm has to fix. W-2 and 1099 turnaround Jan 31 deadline pressure; firms that miss lose entire relationship. Portal usability for employees pay stub and W-2 access without support tickets. Owner reasonable compensation guidance a value-add most S-corp owners want but few firms deliver. Every one of these has a price. A CPA firm's payroll service line should be priced on reliability and integration promise, not on vendor markup alone. In-house delivery vs. white-label referral Every CPA firm eventually decides whether to run payroll in-house on firm's Gusto or QBO account, or to refer clients to a payroll partner and take a referral fee. In-house delivery. Firm holds vendor relationship, owns client communication, and controls workflow. Higher margin per client (40–50% gross) but requires trained staff and workflow discipline. Break-even is typically 15–25 payroll clients. White-label referral. Firm refers clients to Gusto Pro, ADP Accountant Program, or a specialty partner. Firm collects a referral fee ($50–$200 per client per year) but doesn't do work. Zero delivery risk, minimal margin. Best for firms with fewer than 10 payroll-eligible clients or firms that don't want service line to grow into a business. Hybrid. Firm runs payroll for anchor clients (10+ employees, multi-state) and refers small single-owner engagements. Most established firms end up here. The pricing conversation is different in each model. In-house firms price against their own delivery cost. Referral firms price against vendor's list price (usually adding zero markup, taking only referral). How Finlens fits payroll workflow Payroll delivery involves payroll vendor + general ledger + tax authorities. Finlens is ledger layer between them. Payroll journal entry automation. Gusto, QBO Payroll, Rippling, and ADP export payroll data. Finlens posts gross wages, employer taxes, employee withholdings, benefits deductions, and 401(k) contributions to QBO as separate journal entries every pay period. Tax liability reconciliation. Employer payroll taxes (Social Security, Medicare, FUTA, SUTA) accrue to correct liability accounts and clear when payments are made. Multi-state accrual. State withholding and SUI accruals are split by state for multi-state clients so return prep and quarterly filings are straightforward. Owner reasonable compensation flag. S-corp shareholder wages are tagged in ledger with an annual review flag at year-end. Payroll-to-P&L reconciliation. Wages by department, by class, or by job flow from payroll journal to P&L, so firm can produce a labor cost report by dimension without a separate spreadsheet. Finlens does not process payroll Gusto, ADP, and QBO Payroll continue to run vendor side. Finlens is ledger reconciliation layer that keeps payroll clean once it lands in QBO. Conclusion Payroll pricing is a delivery-cost question, not a vendor-invoice question. The vendor invoice is floor; firm's labor is substance. Under $250/mo bundled for a 10-employee client is almost always a loss. $250/mo price floor · 10 EEs 40%+ target gross margin 12 add-ons priced separately Payroll pricing too low? Finlens posts payroll journals from Gusto, ADP, or QBO Payroll cleanly to QBO, splits multi-state accruals, and produces the labor cost data the firm needs to price and defend the next engagement. Book a Walkthrough → See how it works → see how Finlens posts Gusto, QBO Payroll, or Rippling payroll journal to QBO cleanly every pay period, splits multi-state accruals, and produces labor cost reporting firm needs to price its next client. Bring file for client whose payroll journal hits QBO as one lump gross wages entry, whose multi-state withholdings sit in one account, and whose S-corp reasonable compensation review last happened three years ago. That's file this workflow is built for. Frequently asked questions How should a CPA firm price a new payroll client? Start with a bundled fixed monthly quote based on employee count and payroll frequency. Reference market benchmark ($250–$500/mo for a 10-employee bi-weekly client is defensible). Adjust up for multi-state, garnishments, workers comp integration, or benefits admin. Should payroll be a loss leader for firm? No. A payroll service line that runs at negative margin pulls practice's attention away from higher-margin advisory work and consumes staff time. Every payroll engagement should carry at least 30% gross margin at steady state. What's break-even employee count to run payroll in-house? Typically 15–25 clients across firm's book. Below that, fixed overhead (compliance updates, software subscriptions, training) is not covered. Above that, marginal cost per client drops and service line becomes profitable. When does a client outgrow a CPA firm's payroll service? Usually at 50+ employees with multi-state operations or when a full HR function is needed. At that point, a PEO or a dedicated HRIS (Rippling, Justworks) is usually right referral. What add-ons are most often underpriced? Multi-state payroll, garnishments, and workers comp pay-as-you-go integration. These consume staff time and require specialty knowledge. Every firm should price them separately. How much do CPA firms typically make per payroll client? For a well-run practice, $150–$400/mo in gross margin per client, depending on complexity. A firm with 30 payroll clients averaging $250/mo margin is running a $90K/yr service line. The authoritative compliance reference for withholding, deposit, and reporting rules that drive delivery cost is IRS Publication 15 Employer's Tax Guide . title: Brynn Carnesecca Dies at 21: Remembering the Life, Service, and Legacy of Former Miss American Fork
summary: Former Miss American Fork Brynn Carnesecca has died at age 21. Learn about her pageant journey, journalism career, community service, and the legacy she leaves behind. Brynn Carnesecca, the former Miss American Fork 2024 and a rising young journalist from Utah, has died at the age of 21. Known for her dedication to community service, storytelling, and helping others, Brynn’s life touched many people throughout her community and beyond. According to her family, Brynn died by suicide on Sunday.
body_text: Former Miss American Fork Brynn Carnesecca has died at age 21. Learn about her pageant journey, journalism career, community service, and the legacy she leaves behind. Brynn Carnesecca, the former Miss American Fork 2024 and a rising young journalist from Utah, has died at the age of 21. Known for her dedication to community service, storytelling, and helping others, Brynn’s life touched many people throughout her community and beyond. According to her family, Brynn died by suicide on Sunday. Her mother, Michele Carnesecca, shared that she hopes her daughter will be remembered not only for the circumstances of her death, but for the meaningful life she created through kindness, leadership, and service. “She is more than what happened to her,” Michele said, emphasizing that Brynn’s accomplishments, relationships, and positive influence represent the true story of her life. A candlelight vigil was held at the American Fork Amphitheater to honor Brynn’s memory, bringing together friends, family members, community leaders, and people whose lives were impacted by her work. A Bright Presence in the Miss American Fork and Miss Utah Community Brynn Carnesecca earned the title of Miss American Fork in 2024, beginning a journey that highlighted her passion for leadership and community involvement. During the Miss Utah competition, she was recognized by fellow contestants with the Miss Congeniality Award, an honor that reflected her supportive personality and the connections she built with others. The Miss Utah Scholarship Organization remembered Brynn as someone who brought positivity and warmth to both the Miss Utah and Miss American Fork programs. In a statement, the organization highlighted her kindness, friendship, and commitment to serving people across Utah. The current Miss American Fork titleholder also shared a tribute, remembering Brynn as someone who offered encouragement, celebrated others, and made people feel valued. She described Brynn’s impact as leaving a lasting example for future titleholders. Brynn Carnesecca’s Commitment to Community Service Beyond pageantry, Brynn dedicated much of her time to creating programs designed to bring people together and encourage understanding. During her Miss Utah service initiative, Brynn founded Envelopes of Hope , a program focused on connecting community members with incarcerated individuals through written letters. The goal of the project was to create opportunities for empathy, conversation, and human connection. Brynn previously explained that the program helped people understand different life experiences and encouraged meaningful relationships between individuals who might otherwise never interact. Through Envelopes of Hope, she hoped to show that communication and compassion could create positive change. The project became one of the most important examples of her belief in service and the power of kindness. The Utah Miss Amazing organization, where Brynn volunteered as a “buddy,” also honored her contributions. The organization said her compassion and genuine care for others made a lasting impression on everyone she met. A Young Journalist With a Passion for Storytelling In addition to her service work, Brynn built a promising career in journalism. She used storytelling as a way to highlight people, share important community issues, and give others a voice. Brynn worked with several Utah publications and gained experience through internships and reporting opportunities. Her journalism work included contributions to the American Fork Citizen, Lehi Free Press, and Brigham Young University’s Daily Universe. She also completed internships with Utah Valley Magazine, Good Things Utah, and KSL. During her time in journalism, Brynn was recognized as someone who cared deeply about the stories she covered and the people behind them. Her reporting reflected the same qualities that defined her community work: curiosity, empathy, and a desire to connect with others. Remembering Brynn’s Many Talents Friends, family, and supporters have remembered Brynn not only for her achievements but also for her personality, creativity, and dedication. A memorial fundraising campaign described her as an accomplished pianist, journalist, and the creator of Envelopes of Hope. The campaign was created to help support funeral expenses and memorial arrangements for her family. Supporters have contributed to honor Brynn’s memory and recognize the positive influence she had during her 21 years. While her passing has brought deep sadness to those who knew her, many have chosen to focus on the impact she made. Her work in journalism, pageantry, volunteer service, and community outreach continues to represent the values she cared about. Brynn Carnesecca’s Legacy of Kindness and Connection Brynn Carnesecca’s story is one of achievement, compassion, and dedication to others. From earning the title of Miss American Fork to creating a service initiative and pursuing journalism, she spent much of her life encouraging connection between people. Those who knew Brynn describe her as someone who supported others, celebrated their successes, and looked for ways to make her community stronger. Her legacy will continue through the people she inspired, the programs she created, and the stories she shared. As family members and friends remember Brynn, they hope her life will be viewed through the lens of her kindness, creativity, and commitment to helping others. Source: NTD Television, KSL, KSTU, statements from Miss Utah and related community organizations, and publicly available memorial information. title: Lettuce Crisis in the US: Food Safety Scare and Rising Costs Put Restaurants Under Pressure
summary: The US restaurant industry is facing a difficult period as concerns over lettuce safety combine with rising ingredient costs. A nationwide Cyclospora outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce has caused thousands of illnesses and increased worries among customers, especially those who regularly visit salad-focused restaurants and fast-food chains. The outbreak, which began in late June 2026, has affected consumer confidence at a time when restaurants are already dealing with higher food expen
body_text: The US restaurant industry is facing a difficult period as concerns over lettuce safety combine with rising ingredient costs. A nationwide Cyclospora outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce has caused thousands of illnesses and increased worries among customers, especially those who regularly visit salad-focused restaurants and fast-food chains. The outbreak, which began in late June 2026, has affected consumer confidence at a time when restaurants are already dealing with higher food expenses. While health officials continue investigating the exact sources of contamination, businesses that depend heavily on fresh lettuce have experienced a noticeable impact. According to health authorities, the initial investigation connected the outbreak to shredded iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell locations in several US states, including Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia. As more cases were reported, investigators expanded their focus to additional states, including Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Pennsylvania. Taco Bell responded by voluntarily removing shredded iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms from its US restaurants on July 17. The company’s decision was part of efforts to protect customers while health officials continued their investigation. Restaurants Experience Declining Customer Visits The lettuce-related health concerns have affected restaurant traffic, particularly for businesses associated with fresh salads and vegetable-based meals. Market research data from Placer.ai showed that visits to Taco Bell locations across the country dropped significantly by late July. The decline reflected growing customer caution following reports of illnesses connected to contaminated lettuce. Food safety experts have suggested that the situation may involve more than one source. Craig Hedberg, a food safety expert at the University of Minnesota, noted that the increasing number of reported cases indicated a more complicated outbreak investigation. As officials continue gathering information, other restaurant chains that rely heavily on fresh produce have also experienced customer concerns, even though they have not been directly linked to the outbreak. Salad-focused brands, including Chopt and Sweetgreen, reported changes in customer behavior. Chopt saw a decline in visits during the outbreak period, while Sweetgreen experienced lower weekly spending compared with the same period in the previous year. Sweetgreen stated that none of its ingredients had been connected to the outbreak and emphasized that the company follows strict food safety procedures, including ingredient tracking from farms to restaurants. Rising Lettuce Prices Add More Pressure The food safety concerns come during a challenging time for the lettuce supply chain. Restaurants have already been dealing with increased ingredient costs caused by weather conditions, transportation expenses, and supply shortages. Government data shows that iceberg lettuce prices increased significantly during the first half of 2026. Fresh lettuce prices were also considerably higher compared with the previous year, adding pressure to restaurants that use large quantities of greens. Several factors contributed to the price increase. Agricultural experts explained that unusually hot weather in Arizona affected lettuce production earlier in the year. The warmer conditions caused crops to mature faster than expected, creating supply shortages before California’s growing season could fully increase availability. Transportation costs have also played a role. Lettuce requires careful handling and continuous refrigeration from farms to grocery stores and restaurants. Higher fuel and logistics expenses have made the entire supply chain more expensive. For restaurants, the combination of higher prices and customer concerns creates a difficult situation. Businesses must maintain food quality and safety standards while managing increased operational costs. Lettuce Has Faced Food Safety Challenges Before The current Cyclospora outbreak is not the first time lettuce has been connected to major food safety concerns. In 2018, romaine lettuce was linked to multiple E. coli outbreaks associated with growing regions in Arizona and California. Those incidents led to recalls, consumer warnings, and increased discussions about improving safety practices throughout the produce industry. These previous events have encouraged restaurants, farmers, and regulators to strengthen monitoring systems. Modern food safety efforts include better traceability programs, improved farming practices, and faster responses when contamination is suspected. However, leafy greens remain challenging to manage because they are often eaten raw. Unlike foods that are cooked at high temperatures, salads and fresh vegetables may not have a final preparation step that eliminates harmful bacteria or parasites. Consumers Become More Careful About Fresh Foods Following reports of illnesses, many consumers are becoming more selective about where they buy salads and fresh produce. Food safety has become an increasingly important factor when choosing restaurants. Experts say transparency and communication are essential during food-related health events. Restaurants that provide clear information about ingredient sourcing, safety procedures, and response actions may be better positioned to maintain customer trust. The outbreak also highlights the importance of supply chain monitoring. From farms and transportation companies to restaurants and retailers, every stage plays a role in protecting consumers. What This Means for the Restaurant Industry The lettuce crisis demonstrates how quickly food safety concerns can affect businesses. A single ingredient issue can influence customer behavior across an entire category, even impacting companies that are not involved in the outbreak. Restaurants may need to review their supplier relationships, improve tracking systems, and prepare stronger communication strategies for future incidents. At the same time, customers are likely to continue demanding safer and more transparent food production practices. As fresh food remains a major part of modern dining trends, maintaining confidence in ingredients will remain a priority for the restaurant industry. The ongoing investigation into the Cyclospora outbreak will determine the full scope of the contamination and whether additional sources are identified. Until then, restaurants and consumers are closely watching developments while navigating a challenging period for one of America’s most common food ingredients. Source The Independent, Associated Press, US Food and Drug Administration updates, market research information from Placer.ai and industry comments from food safety and agricultural experts. Disclaimer This article is a written summary created for informational purposes only. It does not represent medical, legal, or official public health advice. Readers should refer to official health authorities and verified government updates for the latest information about food safety warnings, recalls, and outbreak investigations.

title: Quantum computing and identity security: Two problems, one imperative
summary: Quantum computing introduces immediate risks to non-human identity and long-term decryption threats. Learn how security leaders can prepare today with Okta.
body_text: Topics Cybersecurity , Non-Human Identities , Okta Platform , Security Table of Contents Share Ready to make Identity a business advantage? Sign up today. Get started Key Takeaways Quantum computing creates two distinct identity security risks: One immediate and one long-term Immediate risk: Active quantum workloads rely on ungoverned non-human identities (NHIs), creating immediate and exploitable vulnerability in many enterprises right now Long-term risk: Known as “Harvest Now, Decrypt Later,” adversaries are actively collecting encrypted data and planning to decrypt it within 10 years using quantum capabilities Security leaders can secure their quantum workloads and cryptographic foundations for the future with Okta’s Blueprint for the Secure Agentic Enterprise Quantum computing is probably already running in your enterprise. And the identities behind those workloads? They’re likely ungoverned. This is a security problem you need to address now. And it doesn’t stop there. You must also begin planning for post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) standards today to future-proof against tomorrow’s decryption threats. Read on to discover the two identity security concerns for quantum computing and why both deserve a seat at the CISO's table in 2026. What is quantum computing—and how does it affect identity security? Quantum computing is a new class of computing that harnesses quantum physics to solve problems classical computers cannot, making them exponentially more powerful for certain tasks. This includes breaking the encryption algorithms that protect enterprise identity systems today. Quantum computing is not just a technology topic; it’s also a security topic. And because every quantum workload authenticates with an identity, identity teams sit at the center of this issue. Two quantum challenges, one identity blind spot The security challenge of quantum computing spans two distinct, yet equally critical timelines that both require the attention of security leaders today: Quantum computing workloads are currently operating commercially with non-human identities (NHIs), but the majority of NHIs are ungoverned Attackers are harvesting encrypted data at this moment, counting on quantum computers powerful enough to decrypt this data in the 2030s Challenge 1: Governing non-human identities in active quantum workloads Quantum computing is already an active enterprise workload. Research teams, data science groups, and optimization engineers across the financial services, pharmaceuticals, logistics, and materials science industries are actively running workloads on platforms like IBM Quantum, AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, and Google Quantum AI. And each of these workloads authenticates using an identity. These are not human users logging in through a browser. They're automated pipelines, Jupyter notebooks running scheduled jobs, CI/CD systems submitting circuits, and orchestration scripts moving data between classical and quantum processors. In identity terms, these are non-human identities (NHIs), and they represent one of the fastest-growing and least-governed attack surfaces in enterprise IT. Okta’s Businesses at Work 2026 survey showed 650% year-over-year growth in centrally managed service accounts used by SaaS apps, services, agents, and tools. Still, only 10% of organizations report having a well-developed strategy to manage them. Five critical identity gaps in current quantum workloads By definition, NHIs don’t have a human connected to them. This makes them prone to the same risky patterns security teams have spent years trying to eliminate for human identities, such as shared credentials and excessive standing access. Those same issues for NHIs also apply to quantum computing workloads: Long-lived API keys and tokens: Some quantum service integrations use static credentials that persist for months or years, with no automatic rotation No enterprise single sign-on (SSO) integration: Some platforms lack native support for Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) or OpenID Connect (OIDC) federation, forcing teams to manage separate credential stores No support for OAuth-based access delegation: Some platforms require long-lived API keys instead of short-lived OAuth tokens, increasing the blast radius if credentials leak Limited visibility: Security teams often lack a centralized view of which NHIs are accessing quantum resources, what permissions they hold, or when they last authenticated No policy-based access controls: Access decisions are binary (key valid or not) rather than contextual (is this the right workload, at the right time, from the right environment?) Challenge 2: Mitigating the "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" cryptographic threat While you secure your current workloads, you must also address the long-term threat to your cryptographic foundation. You don’t worry about the security of identity transactions you rely on today because encryption protects them. The encryption depends on mathematical problems that would take classical computers millions of years to solve. But a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could break today’s encryption in as little as a week. While no such computer exists today, the cryptographic community broadly agrees that this capability will emerge within the next 5 to 15 years. This is the "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" (HNDL) reality. Adversaries are actively intercepting and storing encrypted traffic today, predicting that quantum computers will eventually have the processing power to break current encryption standards. Healthcare, pharmaceutical, and financial services organizations handle sensitive data with long-term retention requirements and long-horizon timelines. For example, the development of a new drug takes an average of 10-15 years . If an adversary captures encrypted authentication tokens, session data, or federated identity assertions today, they may be able to decrypt that data in 2030 or 2035. For organizations handling classified information, long-lived trade secrets, or sensitive personal data, the window for action can’t wait until the next decade. But the risk isn’t limited to specific industries. In August 2024, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalized its first set of PQC standards . Every organization must begin planning to adopt these new PQC algorithms well before quantum computers can decrypt data in real time. Comparison: The two quantum identity imperatives Risk dimension Challenge 1: Non-human identity hygiene Challenge 2: Harvest Now, Decrypt Later Timeline Immediate/active quantum workloads 5-15 year decryption horizon Primary targets Quantum workload APIs, automated pipelines, orchestration scripts Intercepted session data, SAML assertions, tokens Core vulnerability Ungoverned static keys and standing access RSA and ECC Remediation standard Federated SSO, OAuth tokens, just-in-time access NIST PQC Standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205) Okta's approach: Securing identity across both quantum issues Okta occupies a unique position in this landscape. As a leading independent, neutral identity platform , we secure access across a variety of environments, clouds, on-premises systems, and SaaS applications. We're not tied to a single hyperscaler's ecosystem. This independence is foundational to our approach to both near- and medium-term quantum identity challenges. As with cloud computing, organizations will work with multiple providers; no single vendor is likely to "win" the quantum space. This makes platform-neutral identity an operational requirement, not a luxury. If your identity layer is locked into a single provider's ecosystem, you inherit that provider's blind spots. Okta’s independence allows you to enforce a consistent security policy across environments as your quantum strategy matures. A three-part framework for non-human identity governance Every organization should ask three foundational questions about any automated workload accessing enterprise resources, including quantum computing: Who and what is accessing which resources? Ask your team not just who and what have access to your enterprise resources, but what they are doing with that access—including quantum computing workloads. Is that access appropriate? Once you can see a workload, you need to map every resource it can reach, and enforce access policies such as least privilege and just-in-time credentials. What happens when something changes? Knowing where workloads are and what they can connect to isn't enough if you can't control and cut off what they actually do. If a researcher leaves, a project ends, or an attacker compromises a credential, you need to revoke access instantly across all quantum platforms. For most organizations today, the honest answer to all three questions about quantum computing workloads is "we don't know." Solving challenge 1: How Okta secures identity across classical and quantum systems Quantum computing workloads authenticate exactly like any other NHI, which means the same enterprise-grade controls apply directly. Enterprise SSO for non-human workloads: Federate quantum computing access through your existing identity provider, reducing shadow credentials Short-lived, scoped tokens: Replace long-lived API keys with tokens that expire in minutes or hours, dramatically reducing the blast radius of credential compromise Policy-based access controls: Define who (or what) can access which quantum resources, under what conditions, with contextual signals like time, location, and risk score Centralized visibility: A single pane of glass showing all NHIs accessing quantum services across IBM, AWS, Azure, and Google Lifecycle management: Automatically provision and deprovision quantum computing access as projects start and end, teams change, or risk posture shifts This is the cross-cloud advantage. Organizations using multiple quantum providers, which is increasingly common as teams evaluate different hardware architectures, need an identity layer that spans all of them. A platform-native identity solution from a single hyperscaler only covers that hyperscaler's quantum service. Okta covers all the leading hyperscalers. Solving challenge 2: Okta’s two-phase roadmap for post-quantum cryptography Okta is also actively mitigating the long-term threat to the cryptographic foundation of identity. We’ve defined a two-phase roadmap to prepare our customers for a PQC world: Phase 1: Protect our customers (edge and federation) We are implementing Hybrid Key Exchange (HKE), which combines existing algorithms in parallel with the NIST-standardized PQC algorithms. This protects your identities today and against HNDL attacks, and, critically, maintains compatibility with your existing environment. Phase 2: Enable the ecosystem We are equipping the Okta Integration Network and our administrative tooling to support a seamless transition. This includes providing the administrative controls to update tenants to PQC-ready standards as they become the new default, helping ensure your organization can migrate seamlessly. Five immediate action steps for security leaders Quantum computing's identity implications are a current priority. Here's where to start: Inventory your NHIs touching quantum services. You can't secure what you can't see. Map every API key, service account, and automated credential accessing quantum computing platforms. Eliminate long-lived tokens. Migrate to short-lived, federated credentials wherever possible. This is good hygiene regardless of quantum risk. Apply the three-question framework. For every quantum workload, ask: Who is accessing what? Is that access appropriate? What happens when something changes? Audit your cryptographic exposure. Catalog where your identity infrastructure uses RSA and elliptic curve cryptography (ECC). Understand your exposure to HNDL attacks. Verify vendor PQC readiness. Ask your vendors for their PQC roadmap. If they don't have one, that's a red flag. The quantum era will reward organizations that treat identity as the control plane for all workloads: human and non-human, classical and quantum, today and tomorrow. The time to build that foundation is now. Secure your agentic enterprise As autonomous workloads and AI agents scale across your environment at machine speed, treating them as first-class identities is the only way to close emerging security gaps. Protect your organization before they scale out of control. Map your environment and build a secure, resilient foundation with our Blueprint for the Secure Agentic Enterprise . Any mention in this blog of solutions, features, functionalities, certifications, authorizations, or attestations that are not currently Generally Available or have not yet been obtained may not be delivered or obtained on time or at all. We assume no obligation to deliver on such items and you should not rely on them to make your purchase decisions. About the Author David Skyberg Director, Product Management David Skyberg leads Okta Product Management for US Public Sector at Okta. He has decades of experience delivering world-class Security and IAM products. Prior to arriving at Okta, David worked for industry-leading companies such as Capital One, Ping Identity, Microsoft, and RSA Security. In this leadership role, he serves as a strategic advisor on product strategy, solution design, architecture, and engineering for various internal and external stakeholders, including Okta's top global customers. Sandeep also works with Industry Analysts, VCs, and other industry peers on the strategic advisory front. Prior to joining Okta, Sandeep worked for Oracle/Sun Microsystems, HP, Accenture, and GE, leading programs to mitigate security risks in large-scale enterprise service integrations. His multifaceted expertise in AI security, enterprise solution architecture, identity, and cybersecurity, coupled with his business acumen, enables him to engage with executives and technical champions to keep security solutions simple, up to date, and relevant. title: Greenwich LifeSciences Extends Lock-up of Directors and Officers to January 31, 2027
body_text: Greenwich LifeSciences Extends Lock-up of Directors and Officers to January 31, 2027 Download as PDF August 10, 2026 6:00am EDT STAFFORD, Texas, Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Greenwich LifeSciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GLSI) (the "Company"), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on its Phase III clinical trial, FLAMINGO-01, which is evaluating Fast Track designated GLSI-100, an immunotherapy to prevent breast cancer recurrences, today announced that its Board of Directors has extended the lock-up of the shares owned by the Company's directors, officers, and existing pre-IPO investors to January 31, 2027 which is approximately 76 months from the date of the Company's IPO. During this period, current officers, directors and certain shareholders will not be able to sell their shares of the Company's common stock unless otherwise modified by the Board of Directors. After January 31, 2027, the quantity of these locked-up shares that can be sold daily and over various periods of time will be restricted under a leak-out plan unless otherwise modified by the Board of Directors. The Board could choose to end all or a small percentage of the 100% lock-up at any time for any reason, including prior to any data announcements, interim analyses, strategic transactions, such as an acquisition or partnership, or financial transactions, such as royalty or strategic investor transactions that provide a potential bridge to commercialization. The Board could also choose to implement a pre-determined leak-out plan and/or a 10b5-1 selling program at any time for any reason that allows for the organized independent selling of some of the locked-up shares by a third party over a specified period of time. Such decisions may or may not be announced at the time of the board's decision. CEO Snehal Patel commented, "We attended and presented at the BIO conference in June 2026 and plan to attend the BIO-Europe conference later this year, where strategic and financing transactions can be originated or concluded. With the further derisking of the Phase III clinical trial, more than doubling of enrollment and event rate, interest from leading clinicians and hospitals in up to 200 sites in the US and Europe, screening of over 1,500 patients, and the transformation of the interim analysis into a big pharma like study similar in design to recent large breast cancer studies, we are expecting a continued up-tick in the quantity and seriousness of such discussions." About Greenwich LifeSciences, Inc. Greenwich LifeSciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of GP2, an immunotherapy to prevent breast cancer recurrences in patients who have previously undergone surgery. GP2 is a 9 amino acid transmembrane peptide of the HER2 protein, a cell surface receptor protein that is expressed in a variety of common cancers, including expression in 75% of breast cancers at low (1+), intermediate (2+), and high (3+ or over-expressor) levels. Greenwich LifeSciences has commenced a Phase III clinical trial, FLAMINGO-01. body_text: Hamilton, Bermuda, August 11, 2026 Himalaya Shipping Ltd. (“Himalaya,” “Himalaya Shipping” or the “Company”) announces preliminary unaudited results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026. Highlights for the Second Quarter of 2026 Total time-charter revenues of $53.3 million, which represents average time charter equivalent (“TCE”) earnings of approximately $50,600 per day, gross[1]. Average Baltic 5TC 180 Capesize Index was $36,303 per day. Net income of $24.6 million and EBITDA[2] of $44.0 million. Entered into a new time charter agreement for the Mount Emai for a period of 12 to 14 months at an index-linked rate, reflecting a significant premium to the Baltic 5TC 180 Capesize index. Converted the index-linked time charters for four vessels to fixed-rate time charters at an average rate of approximately $56,500 per day, gross, for the month of June 2026. Cash distributions of $0.15, $0.22 and $0.22 per common share for April, May and June 2026, respectively. Subsequent Events Achieved TCE earnings for July 2026 of approximately $51,200 per day, gross. Declared a cash distribution of $0.22 per common share for July 2026. Entered into a new time charter agreement for the Mount Aconcagua for a period of 16 to 18 months at an index-linked rate, reflecting a significant premium to the Baltic 5TC 180 Capesize index. Converted the index-linked time charters for two vessels to fixed-rate time charters at an average rate of approximately $51,200 per day, gross, from August 1,2026 to December 31, 2026. Himalaya Shipping Ltd. is an independent bulk carrier company, incorporated in Bermuda. Himalaya Shipping has twelve vessels in operation. title: Shannon (EINN) GA security procedures: New arrival and departure requirements
summary: Shannon Airport (EINN) has introduced new security procedures affecting how certain general aviation flights are handled on arrival and how passengers, crew and baggage are processed before departure.
body_text: Universal Aviation Ireland reports that Shannon Airport (EINN) has introduced new security procedures affecting how certain general aviation flights are handled on arrival and how passengers, crew and baggage are processed before departure. The key distinction for arriving flights is now whether passengers, crew and hold baggage were screened at the airport of origin under a security standard recognized by Ireland. Flights that do not meet those requirements may face additional controls after arrival, including parking in a controlled area and restrictions on access to the aircraft. For departures, the former dedicated GA/VIP screening process is no longer available. Passengers, crew and baggage must now pass through Central Search in Shannon’s main terminal. For operators, this means both the origin of the flight and the security status of the passengers, crew and baggage need to be considered before the mission reaches Shannon. title: 10 Best Low-Code Platforms in 2026: Reviewed and Ranked
summary: The top 10 low-code platforms for 2026 compared on features, pricing, AI capabilities, and use cases. Find the right tool before you commit to a stack.
body_text: Most teams pick a low code platform the wrong way. They sign up for the one with the best-looking demo, build for six months, and then discover the platform cannot handle their actual requirements or that switching would mean starting from scratch. The market is crowded with tools that look similar on the surface but diverge sharply when it comes to what you can build, how much it costs at scale, and whether you own what you create. This guide cuts through that. We reviewed 10 platforms against the same criteria (build flexibility, backend connectivity, pricing predictability, and code ownership) and ranked them based on what matters for teams building real production applications. What is a Low Code Platform? A low code platform is a visual development environment that allows users to build applications through graphical user interfaces and configuration instead of traditional hand coding. Think of it as a set of powerful building blocks. You drag and drop components, connect data sources, and define logic visually, which the platform then translates into code. This approach significantly speeds up the development process. Low code can accelerate development by up to 10 times compared to traditional methods. This efficiency is why the market reception has been overwhelmingly positive, with organizations recognizing the power to innovate faster and reduce backlogs. How to Choose a Low Code Platform The right platform depends on what you are building, who will maintain it, and how much flexibility you need long-term. A tool that works for a simple internal dashboard will break under the requirements of a production SaaS product. Before committing, answer these questions: What are you building? Internal tool, client portal, or customer-facing SaaS each require different levels of complexity. Who will build and maintain it? Some platforms require JavaScript knowledge to go beyond the basics. Others are low-code. Do you need to own your code? If the platform does not offer export, you are locked in. Factor that into the long-term cost. What is your backend? Make sure the platform connects to your existing data sources, whether that is Supabase, Xano, PostgreSQL, or a custom API. What are your compliance requirements? GDPR, HIPAA, and data residency rules may require self-hosting. Not all platforms support it properly. Costs and Pricing: Typical Tiers and Hidden Gotchas Most platforms follow a tiered model: free for evaluation, $20 to $200 per month for professional use, and custom enterprise pricing. The advertised price is rarely what you end up paying. Watch out for: Per-seat pricing that gets expensive fast as your team grows Feature gating that locks custom domains, role-based access, or audit logs behind higher tiers Usage limits on rows, API calls, or monthly workflow runs No code export meaning you pay a switching cost if you ever want to leave Hosting fees charged separately on top of the base subscription Open Source vs Proprietary Low Code Open source platforms give you full control: self-host, modify, and avoid licensing fees. The trade-off is that you own the infrastructure, updates, and security patches too. For teams without DevOps resources, that overhead is often underestimated. Proprietary platforms are smoother to use but create dependency. If the vendor raises prices or shuts down, your options are limited. A hybrid approach, like WeWeb, gives you the polished managed experience with the option to self-host or export a clean Vue.js codebase if you ever need to leave. For anything you plan to run long-term, that exit option matters. Governance and Best Practices for Sustainable Low Code Low code makes it easy to build fast and even easier to create a maintenance problem six months later. A few habits prevent that. Name everything consistently : components, variables, workflows. Agree on conventions before you build, not after. Define who can build what : clear ownership prevents five people building five versions of the same thing. Document non-obvious decisions as you make them, especially workarounds. Review before going to production : a simple sign-off step catches most citizen developer mistakes. Audit every six months : unused apps, duplicated components, and bloated workflows accumulate quietly. Trends in Low Code (2026) to Future Proof Your Choice Low code is moving fast. The platforms that look competitive today may fall behind within a year if they are not positioned for where the market is going. AI is becoming native , not a bolt-on. The best platforms now generate components, suggest bindings, and flag errors inside the builder itself. Code export is becoming a baseline expectation , not a premium feature. Buyers are more aware of lock-in risk than they were two years ago. Backend-agnostic builders are winning over monolithic all-in-one platforms. Teams want to pair their visual builder with Supabase, Xano, or a custom API rather than accept a built-in database. Self-hosting is no longer an edge case : GDPR, HIPAA, and data residency requirements are making it a serious evaluation criterion. Enterprise adoption is accelerating , pushing platforms to invest in SSO, audit logs, and compliance certifications. How We Evaluated Platforms We focused on what teams actually need to build and maintain production-grade applications, not just what looks good in a demo. Each platform was assessed against the same criteria. Build flexibility : handles complex logic, not just simple forms Backend connectivity : works with REST APIs, GraphQL, Supabase, Xano, and custom databases Code ownership : exports a clean, usable codebase Pricing predictability : modeled at 5, 20, and 50 seats Self-hosting support : documented, not just technically possible Team collaboration : role-based access, version history, shared component libraries Top 10 Low Code Platforms With a clear understanding of what low code can offer, it’s time to dive into the market leaders who are setting the standard. This curated list will help you navigate the crowded marketplace and identify the perfect tool to accelerate your development.
